answer: The soap boiler tests the lye strength of every batch and stamps the batch number on each bar, and the batch book holds the test for every bar sold. A umber bar bought from a pedlar fails the book: at the opal of the stamp the batch number must match the boiler's own test, and a pedlar's bar carries no number at all. Forging a batch means running a soap house for six months, buying tallow and ash, and paying 7,300, while the meadow entry in the batch book is read at every fair, so a bar whose batch was never tested is thrown out.
